mekayis.metin: (تَوَّ) التَّاءُ وَالْوَاوُ كَلِمَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَهِيَ التَّوُّ، وَهُوَ الْفَرْدُ. وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: «الطَّوَافُ تَوٌّ» . وَيُقَالُ سَافَرَ سَفَرًا تَوًّا، وَذَلِكَ أَنْ لَا يُعَرِّجَ، فَإِنْ عَرَّجَ بِمَكَانٍ وَأَنْشَأَ سَفَرًا آخَرَ فَلَيْسَ بِتَوٍّ.

zemahseri.hakikat: فتل الحبل والخيط تواً واحداً أي طاقاً واحداً لا قوى له. وكان تواً، فصار زواً، أي زوجاً معه آخر. وفي الحديث: " الطواف تو والاستجمار تو ".

vikisozluk.baslik: تَوّ • (taww) m (plural أَتْوَاء (ʔatwāʔ))
anlam: a knot, a twist or contortion in a rope; a rope that is twisted of a single strand
instantaneousness, immediacy, onlyness, the condition of having been present just i.e. recently and/or alone

vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: In the sense of a knot from Persian تو (tô, “twist”). In the sense of having been just a borrowing from Egyptian Arabic تَوّ (taww) in its meaning, also Hassaniya Arabic تو (tow, “instant”), Marazīq Tunisian Arabic تاو (tâu, “moment”), in view of Sabaean 𐩻𐩥 (ṯw, “until”) borrowed from Old South Arabian, in its more original meaning present in Andalusian Arabic ثَو ذَا (ṯaw ḏā) or تَو ذَا (taw ḏā, “until now”) and Yemeni Arabic تَو (taw, “in front of”), and following this prepositional character still most notorious with personal suffixes. Possibly corresponding to سَوْفَ (sawfa) and Ge'ez ሶበ (sobä), ሶቤ (sobe, “when”).
